rows.description: A teacher's kindness helped me through a dark year, and I feel deep thanks. Wise: gratitude can coexist with clear eyes; support the good, keep thinking. Harmful: feeling that thanks means never questioning.

rows.description: I found out my teacher lives in luxury and keeps secrets. My heart broke. Wise: grieve the image, keep what truth I learned, and separate the practice from the person. Harmful: dropping every value out of anger.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, fear, gratitude, manipulation, worship

rows.description: I ask my teacher before every decision and feel lost without him. Wise: a good guide builds my judgement, not my dependence; make small choices alone and see that I can. Harmful: outsourcing my whole life.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, manipulation, worship

rows.description: My friend has cut off his family for the ashram and I worry about him. Wise: keep the door open, stay warm, ask curious questions, avoid attacking his teacher. Harmful: ultimatums that push him deeper.

rows.description: Members shower me with attention, meals and "you belong here" in my first week. I feel warm after a lonely year. Wise: enjoy kindness but notice if love is tied to obedience or to cutting off others.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, disillusionment, fear, loyalty, protectiveness

rows.description: I am asked to donate, hand over my phone and stop seeing old friends "for my growth". Wise: these are control signals; keep independent contact, money and a way to leave, and talk to someone outside.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, compassion, disillusionment, fear, loyalty, protectiveness

rows.description: I defend the group even though private doubts are growing. Belonging is strong. Wise: notice which questions I am not allowed to ask; loyalty that forbids thinking is worth examining. Harmful: silencing my doubts.

rows.description: My family begs me to leave the group, and I see them as enemies who do not understand. Wise: listen for love inside their fear, and keep one connection alive even if I disagree. Harmful: cutting them off as told.

rows.description: I finally saw that the group's promises did not match its actions. I feel foolish and grieve years lost. Wise: leaving is brave, not stupid; get support, seek counselling and rebuild slowly. Harmful: self-blame.
